finding: Reference group for dose-response neuropsychiatric analyses
Evacuated from 30km zone; includes Pripyat residents; psychological trauma from displacement
Populations in areas with >555 kBq/m2 Cs-137; mandatory resettlement eventually
Broader contaminated area residents; lower doses but largest population
Psychiatric disorders appeared almost immediately at doses >300 mSv; organic brain syndrome; cognitive impairment
Psychiatric disorders appeared ~2 years post-exposure at doses 50-300 mSv; subclinical cognitive changes; depression
Psychiatric disorders appeared ~10 years post-exposure at <50 mSv; primarily anxiety; stress-related disorders
Excess psychiatric disorder rate in first post-accident year: ~20% above baseline; fear radiation anxiety displacement
Elevated cerebrovascular disease risk at doses >150 mSv; elevated stroke mortality
Depression more prevalent in confirmed ARS cases vs non-confirmed; statistical significance p=0.006; long-term psychiatric sequela of acute radiation syndrome
Retinal angiopathy relative risk: 2.6-2.93 (dose-dependent); radiation effect on small vessels; correlates with cardiovascular endpoints
Cognitive impairment and early dementia: dose-dependent; confounded by stress, alcohol, economic disruption post-Soviet; elevated vs general population

Chernobyl Forum 2005: mental health is the greatest public health problem caused by Chernobyl; far larger burden than radiation-induced cancer; fear of radiation, displacement, loss of livelihood are primary drivers
Elevated suicide rates in evacuated communities (especially Belarus and Ukraine); related to social disruption, unemployment, hopelessness; not directly radiation-caused

Major determinants of poor health in affected populations: stress/anxiety, lifestyle (alcohol tobacco), poverty, poor healthcare access; radiation dose at typical population levels is a minor determinant relative to socioeconomic factors
source: WHO 2006; Chernobyl Forum 2005; PMC8629042 systematic review

finding: LNT projected ~6600 cancer deaths across Europe over 70yr from Chernobyl vs ~700 million expected cancer deaths in same population over same period; radiation contribution <0.01% of total cancer burden
1986 official dose limit for liquidators was 350 mSv; many exceeded this; limit applied but enforcement poor; 1987 limit reduced to 250 mSv after controversy
Ukraine allocates 5-7% of annual government budget for Chernobyl disaster recovery and consequences; total economic losses 1986-2015 estimated >700 billion USD (official estimate)
source: IAEA; Chernobyl News 2026; multiple Ukrainian government sources
